language.reasoning: Resolved primarily English, with the caveat that one review (Wilma) is in Spanish. Evidence for EN: (1) the business's own confirmed Instagram account @beautytuneup_ has an English-only bio ('Lashes, Teeth Whitening, Facials and Brows... Book an appointment by texting or calling') and all ~10 recent post captions read/sampled in this session are in English (e.g. 'Behind every facial, lash set, brow design, and spray tan...', 'Skincare terms, translated', 'The perfect day doesn't exist... but better to be sure'); (2) Groupon's own deal/business description ('A deep cleansing facial targeting those pesky clogged pores...') is English; (3) 3 of 4 review quotes are English, only 1 of 4 is Spanish. Little Havana's clientele does skew Spanish-speaking, and the business likely serves Spanish-speaking walk-ins day to day (hence Wilma's Spanish review and the choice to keep the site bilingual with an ES toggle), but the business's own outward-facing voice (IG, Groupon copy) is consistently English, so English was set as the site's default language rather than overriding to Spanish on demographic assumption alone.

images_curation_note: Instagram feed yielded 19 downloadable real photos/video posters across the 12 most recent posts (pagination beyond that was not attempted; IG's web API returned no further posts without auth). Each was visually opened and inspected one by one. Rejected: several pure text/quote graphics with no photo content ('recharge mode: ON', 'life hack: book a facial'), a posed two-person portrait with no treatment content (personal-style photo, not used anywhere including as a gallery tile, consistent with the 'no selfies/portraits as gallery tiles' rule), 3 educational skincare-terms text-carousel slides, and 3 more procedure photos with a closed-eye subject AND a text caption overlay baked into the image (rejected primarily for the on-image caption text, which the quality gate prohibits in gallery). 4 of the 8 used images required a rectangular crop (via PIL) to physically remove a caption text band before they qualified as clean, real, non-text photos; this is a crop of an unaltered real photo, not a fabrication. 3 further real photos were sourced from Google Photos via the business's confirmed Google Place ID (reached through an Atly aggregator mirror after direct Yelp/Google Maps scraping was blocked). All 8 final images show either a finished/open-eye result, a clean real interior, or a legitimate in-progress treatment with no gore/irritation/clutter, per the visual quality gate.
